claim: Two separate 400-tick synthetic combat runs reproduce all mapped guest-memory hashes,87 enumerated ARM64 registers and typed/order-preserving adapter observations at every tick.
scope: A stronger repeatability observation for the existing synthetic Knight/KingTower fixture; not a complete VM snapshot, Android reference oracle, or byte-identical full battle proof.

serialization_audit.v1_weaknesses: The first prototype merged some concrete Python types and dict insertion orders; it omitted aliases and some registers. Its matching game observations did not establish complete host-state capture.
serialization_audit.v2_changes: Preserve concrete allowed types, dict/Counter iteration order, observed set order, float bits, cycles and cross-attribute container aliases; hash tick and explicit runtime configuration; reject unknown types.

limitations: Synthetic empty 5x5 arena and selected globals materialized from CSV; original arena initializer runs but full arena data is absent
Original default mode constructor, two synthetic player-level records and placeholder account IDs; full match context initialization absent
Only supplied Knight/KingTower/rarity/global-ID/tag assets loaded; optional references in the complete manifest may remain unresolved
KingTower starting-action pointer resolves and original enqueue path runs, but normal INACTIVE/activation semantics are unverified
Original context phase setter is called once explicitly; top-level match scheduler and timing contract not established
Bounded allocation/free without reclamation, standard libc primitive models, isolated uncontended mutex/gettid models; selected original shipped libc++ functions execute
Selected live actor fields, counts and entry traces only; no complete raw-state/event differential oracle
Dead Knight state is marked absent after native removal; residual freed allocation contents are not reported as live state
Only the listed architectural registers are observed; exclusive monitors, pending exception state, unenumerated registers and opaque Unicorn internals are not captured.
Hook registration order, callable/module globals and callback closures are outside this capture. Frozen source hashes identify code but are not a complete execution-state snapshot.
Python process/container internals and immutable-object identity are not represented; observed container contents/order/aliasing are recorded but hash-table capacity/tombstones are not.
Capture requires a stopped single-threaded native boundary; it is not an atomic concurrent snapshot or a validated reset/restore implementation.
The original native test runner, real map and outer match loop are absent from this combat fixture.
Per-region cryptographic hashes are compared, with exact representation and no tolerance; the actual protected guest-memory contents remain private.

synthetic_controls.scope: Read-only stability and negative controls for synthetic memory/register/adapter state; no original game bytes modified
